blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is legal here (never criminalised); there is no legal gender recognition; a small organised LGBTI community operates in the capital; customary-law and church conservatism are present, but there is no documented anti-trans violence pattern.
blindSourceSummaries: A country page on an international LGBTI legal database: documents this country's legal status for same-sex conduct and gender recognition.

NOTE: only the homepage of an international legal-aid trust was retrievable at fetch time (no country-specific page); the trust maps jurisdictions criminalising LGBT people, which include this country.

A foreign government's permanent mission at a UN hub (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the UN Human Rights Council, relevant to this country's international human-rights environment.

A women's organisation (Oct 2016): the national LGBTI organisation and the national women's centre held their first joint LGBTI human-rights workshop (an introduction to LGBTI human rights, SOGIE, health and gender-based violence) at a church hall in the capital - exploring gender stereotypes: 'not conforming to gender roles was the root of discrimination'.

Regional news outlet (Aug 2012): commentary on whether marriage equality recently introduced in a larger regional state could influence this region - in this country gay people face legal challenges such as ineligibility for the same protections as heterosexual couples; consensual activity became legally equal in 2007, but there is no recognition of same-sex unions.

National law-reform commission issues paper (June 2014): a review of the marriage statute - includes one issue on same-sex marriage and its registration, inviting public submissions on how the marriage law treats same-sex marriage.
